name: Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung Scholarship (Studienwerk) — International Students (Master's)

universities: Any state or state-recognized German university

duration: Up to the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of the Master's program; funding typically begins in the 2nd Master's semester
eligibleNationalities: Open to foreign nationals worldwide (including Bangladesh) who are NOT eligible under BAföG §8; EU nationals may also apply. Applicant must be physically residing/studying in Germany and intend to return home afterward.
languageRequirements: Very good German, B2 level, proof required (even if the degree is taught in English). If B2 not yet reached by the deadline, a B1 certificate plus proof of enrolment in an ongoing/upcoming B2 course is accepted.
standardizedTests: Not required (no IELTS/TOEFL/GRE mentioned; German proficiency is the language requirement)
ageLimit: Not stated for the international Master's track, but applicant must not have been in Germany for more than 15 months at the time of application (unless they already did a Bachelor's in Germany or are in university preparation)
applicationFee: Free (online application via portal; no fee mentioned)
fundingCovers: Monthly living-cost stipend (Lebenshaltungsstipendium, based on BAföG rates)
Income-independent study-cost lump sum (Studienkostenpauschale) of currently 300 EUR/month
Health- and care-insurance subsidies (analogous to BAföG)
Optional child-care supplement (Kinderbetreuungszuschlag, analogous to BAföG)
Extensive non-material support: political-education events, summer schools, workshops, seminars, skills training, networks
monthlyStipend: Living-cost base set by BAföG rates plus a 300 EUR/month income-independent study-cost lump sum (exact base figure not published as a single fixed number on the official pages)
bondObligation: No contractual financial bond. The official International Scholarships page states applicants must 'plan to return to their home country after completing their education' — this is a stated expectation only, not an enforceable bond.
renewalConditions: Funding lasts up to the standard period of study; no legal entitlement to funding ('Ein rechtlicher Anspruch auf Förderung besteht nicht'); continued academic performance and engagement expected
benefits: Monthly living-cost stipend based on BAföG rates (Lebenshaltungsstipendium) — does NOT have to be repaid, unlike BAföG
Income-independent study-cost lump sum (Studienkostenpauschale) of currently 300 EUR per month
Subsidies toward health and care insurance (analogous to BAföG)
Optional child-care supplement for scholarship holders with children (analogous to BAföG)
Comprehensive non-material program: political education, summer schools, workshops, symposia, educational trips, skills seminars, and access to 250+ academic confidants/networks
requiredDocuments: Certificate of enrolment/matriculation (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) for winter semester 2026/2027 stating completed subject- and university-semesters and the degree program (or a current admission letter if not yet enrolled)
Tabular CV (in German or English) with full educational history
Proof of social/political engagement (e.g. confirmation letters, event programs from political groups, parties, unions, associations, university bodies, NGOs)
One academic reference/assessment (Gutachten) from a lecturer/professor on your ability and performance (German or English; no template)

Proof of highest educational qualification (e.g. Bachelor's certificate) with final grade; if not in German/English, add a non-certified translation (Bachelor's certificate may be submitted by 01.11.2026 if not yet available, with a current transcript + university confirmation of successful completion)
Current transcript of records from the German university, if available
Extract from the study regulations showing the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit)
Residence permit / visa for Germany (for non-EU citizens) — a Fiktionsbescheinigung is NOT sufficient; may be submitted by 01.04.2026 if not yet held
Proof of German language skills at least at B2 level (or B1 plus proof of an ongoing/upcoming B2 course)

timeline.resultsBy: Selection interviews with a Vertrauensdozent*in run mid-December to February; grants begin the following summer semester (1 April)
timeline.notes: Anchored to 2026-06: as of the verification date the next equivalent round had not yet opened, so dates are from the most recently opened cycle (application round opening 20 Aug 2025, deadline 1 Oct 2025) as published on the official scholarship-application page; the next round is expected around 20 Aug / 1 Oct annually. The general rule stated on the English page is '1 October for grants beginning in the summer semester (1 April) of the next year.'

mustKnow: German proficiency at B2 level is mandatory even for English-taught Master's programs — proof required at application (B1 + ongoing B2 course accepted as a stopgap).

You must already be in Germany to study: applicant must be enrolled (or at least admitted) at a German state/state-recognized university and physically residing in Germany for the studies. This is NOT a scholarship to fund a fresh move from Bangladesh — you apply once you are an international student in Germany.
15-month rule: you must not have been in Germany for more than 15 months at the time of application (unless you already completed a Bachelor's in Germany or are in university preparation).
Return-home expectation: applicants must plan to return to their home country after completing their education (an expectation, not an enforceable bond).
Tuition is NOT reimbursed — the international award is explicitly a living-cost stipend (Lebenshaltungsstipendium); fortunately most German public universities charge little or no tuition.

This international track is Master's only (PhD is a separate program); strong demonstrable social/political engagement aligned with the left-wing aims of the Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung is a core selection criterion, alongside above-average academic performance.

Bachelor's degree must be completed before the deadline; you typically apply while in your 1st Master's semester and funding begins in the 2nd semester. The application portal and forms are German-only.
Multi-stage selection including an interview with a trusted lecturer (Vertrauensdozent*in), Dec–Feb. No legal entitlement to funding.
Study in Great Britain and study abroad in your country of origin/third countries are not fundable.
Cannot hold a part-time job of more than 20 hours/week; for AA-funded international students, earnings up to the minijob limit within the 20h rule are not counted against the stipend.
Family support is limited to an optional child-care supplement (Kinderbetreuungszuschlag) for holders with children — there is no general spouse/dependent relocation or insurance package.
